{ "rules": [
    "Model forecasts are consistently too low in the early 30-day horizon, showing significant undervaluation that gradually converges to match true outcomes",
    "Sentiment strength directly correlates with forecast bias, as high sentiment (1.0) periods show the largest divergence between forecast and true prices",
    "The forecast lag effect is most pronounced at 1-7 day horizons where true prices continue adjusting from recent momentum while forecasts remain anchored to historical means",
    "Mean reversion bias exists in both directions but leans toward undershooting recovery rallies, particularly when sentiment has been strongly bullish",
    "Forecast volatility is systematically lower than true price volatility, especially in the 11-20 day range where model confidence decays relative to actual price uncertainty",
    "Sentiment turning points create the largest forecast errors as models exhibit momentum lag on the opposite side of trends",
    "When sentiment mixes positive and negative (0.5-0.67 range), forecasts become excessively flat compared to the continued price movement in true outcomes" ]
}
